About

Who built this, and why.

I am Paula Silva, Developer Solutions Advisor and Software Latam Leader on the Data & AI team, Global Black Belt for Microsoft Americas. My work spans the full AI transformation journey, from application and legacy modernization to agentic architecture and platform engineering, helping enterprise teams adopt AI-assisted development at scale. Hooks are where an agent stops being a black box and becomes a system you can govern.

This deck is the technical deep dive on GitHub Copilot hooks, rebuilt for the September 2026 hooks reference: the fourteen lifecycle events and their exact input and output contracts, exit codes and fail-open versus fail-closed rules, matchers and the Claude-compatible format, where hooks live and in what order they load, what the cloud agent, VS Code, JetBrains and the GitHub Copilot SDK support, guardrails against destructive commands and prompt injection, quality automation, audit to a SIEM through HTTP hooks, OpenTelemetry, policy hooks and managed settings, and an adoption path with a starter kit and a lab.

It is built as a two to three hour workshop for platform and security engineers and for the developers who will write the first hooks: every part closes with a how-to with real JSON and a scenarios slide, there is a hook decision simulator you run live, and the last part hands the room a ninety day path. Every fact is checked against docs.github.com, the GitHub Copilot CLI changelog and the VS Code docs as of September 2026.
